raw_response:
I've been farming this same cotton land in Quzhou for over 40 years. I know what works here. My 15 mu is all cotton — that's not changing. Cotton suits this land, the market is familiar to me, and at 65 with just my wife and me at home, I'm not taking on the learning curve of a new crop system.

For seed, I'll use hybrid Bt cotton again, same as I've done for the past two decades. The bollworm resistance built into it has saved me enormous labor and cost. When I was young I was out spraying for bollworm five or six times a season. Now I don't have to.

I'll plough deep before planting, like always. Rotary tillage doesn't get the depth cotton roots need. I've tried it. I go back to plough every time.

For fertilizer, I put phosphorus and potassium down as base before planting, with part of the nitrogen. I side-dress the rest of the nitrogen during boll setting — that's when the plant really needs it. I've refined these rates over the years to what my soil here actually responds to.

Irrigation: four times is my standard. Seedling stage if it's dry, flowering, early boll, late boll. The well is reliable. I won't under-irrigate during boll development — that's where yield is made or lost.

Pesticides: even with Bt seed I still have aphids in June and spider mites in August. Five applications is what I typically need — not more, not fewer.

I expect 300 kg of seed cotton per mu in a normal weather year.
